simple.meaning: אַכְזָרִי (ʼakzârîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “terrible.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַכְזָרִי (H394) appears 8 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Proverbs 5:9, with occurrences in Proverbs, Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַכְזָרִי (H394) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַכְזָרִי (H394) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַכְזָרִי (ʼakzârîy) / H394 is traced through Proverbs 5:9, Proverbs 11:17, Proverbs 12:10, Proverbs 17:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H394. akzari אַכְזָרִי adjective cruel , always in this form; — Prov 12:10 ; 17:11 ; Jer 6:23 ; 50:42 , also 30:14 (read א ׳מוּסָר , for מוּסַר ᵑ0 , Gf Gie); as substantive Prov 5:9 ; 11:17 , perhaps also, in apposition with י ׳יוֺם , Isa 13:9 .
